newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour sees small chance of confidence vote win.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour sees small chance of confidence vote win.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party sees little chance of defeating the government if it were to call a confidence vote on European issues, the party's senior parliamentary business manager, Donald Dewar, said on Monday.
"We will make every effort to force a general election, but that involves a judgement that we can win a vote," Labour chief whip Dewar told BBC radio.
"At the moment we have very little chance of doing so," he added.

Dewar was speaking in advance of a statement to parliament by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke forced on the government by Conservative MPs angry that they had no chance to debate documents relating to proposals for a single European currency.

"I think that what we have got to do is to judge whether we can get a motion that we can respectably vote for...and we have got to get into the same lobby to defeat the government, almost certainly some Tory rebels and also the majority of the Northern Ireland MPs," Dewar said.
"Now that is not easy to do but I can assure you that if we think there is a chance of doing it, then we will certainly go for it, and go for it with great energy and enthusiasm."
"If the circumstances arise that allow us to strike that knock-out punch, we will do it. If we have to wait until May...then we will take our chance then," he added.
Prime Minister John Major must call a general election by May 22.
Dewar said the fact Clarke had to make his statement on the day before he unveils his budget "is in itself a measure of the difficulties the government is in".

He called for a debate in parliament on the documents on Friday, before Clarke next week attends a meeting of European Union economic and finance ministers at which they will be discussed. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
